prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to give the best, specific recommendation I’ll need your ZIP code (and whether this is a house or a business, and if it’s an emergency). If you want a quick, general answer now, here’s practical guidance plus a few widely used names in the Houston market.

If you want me to pick a company near you, tell me your ZIP and whether it’s residential or commercial.

General tips for choosing the best HVAC repair company
- Verify credentials: registered with the Texas Dept. of Licensing & Regulation (TDLR) and NATE-certified technicians are good signs.  
- Check reviews: Google, Yelp, BBB, and Angi for recent ratings and complaint history.  
- Ask up front: diagnostic fee, flat-rate vs hourly labor, parts & labor warranties, emergency response time, and whether they pull permits when required.  
- Get 2–3 written estimates for anything beyond a basic repair.  
- Prefer companies that offer maintenance plans if you want long-term reliability.

Local companies in Houston to consider (examples to check in your ZIP)
- John Moore Services — long-established Houston company, does repairs, installs, and maintenance plans.  
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (local franchisees) — national network with local service and 24/7 options.  
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (franchise) — often available for fast service windows and guarantees on response times.  
- Local well-reviewed independent shops — many excellent local HVAC contractors do high-quality work and competitive pricing; searching by ZIP will surface those.

Red flags to avoid
- Unmarked vehicles or techs who refuse to show ID or license.  
- Strong high-pressure sales to replace instead of diagnosing.  
- Cash-only demand or no written estimate.  
- Very low upfront price that later balloons with “unexpected” charges.

Immediate troubleshooting before you call
- Check the thermostat batteries and settings (heat/cool, fan on/auto).  
- Replace or check the air filter.  
- Check the breaker and outdoor unit power switch.  
- Clear debris around the outdoor condenser.  
- If the unit is short-cycling, noisy, or smells like burning, turn it off and call a pro.

If you give your ZIP code and whether this is urgent, I’ll list the top 3–5 highly rated companies near you (with notes on why they’re recommended and what to ask when you call).
